---
title: "Getting started"
---

By the end of this page you will have sent one custom event from a Python script and found it in your Umami dashboard. That is the whole arc: install, configure, send, look. It assumes you already have a running Umami instance, self-hosted or Umami Cloud, with a website registered in it. If you are on Cloud, skim the Cloud section at the end before you configure anything, because one line is different.

## Install

The package on PyPI is `umami-analytics`. The import name is `umami`.

```bash
uv add umami-analytics
# or
pip install umami-analytics
```

A warning that earns its own paragraph: do not run `pip install umami`. That name belongs to an unrelated project that also imports as `umami`. The symptoms are an import that succeeds and functions that are not there, followed by a confused half hour.

The package supports Python 3.10 and newer and depends on `httpx2` and `pydantic`.

## Configure

There is no client object to construct and nothing to pass around. The package is a module with a memory. You tell it three things once, when your application starts, and every later call reads them.

```python
import umami

umami.set_url_base('https://umami.example.com')  # your instance root, without /api
umami.set_website_id('978435e2-7ba1-4337-9860-ec31ece2db60')
umami.set_hostname('example.com')
```

Each of those lines has a story:

- `set_url_base()` goes first, always. It checks that the URL starts with `http://` or `https://` and trims a trailing slash. Leave `/api` off; the package appends the endpoint paths itself, and including it is the most common cause of a 404 on every single call.
- `set_website_id()` takes the id from the Umami dashboard (Settings, Websites, Edit). It becomes the default for every later call, and any call can override it with its own `website_id` argument.
- `set_hostname()` is the hostname stamped on each event. Umami groups traffic by it, so use the domain your visitors type, not the name of the server doing the sending. A hostname of `worker-03.internal` will work, and it will haunt your reports.

Notice what is missing: a login. Sending events needs no credential at all, because Umami's ingestion endpoint is public by design, the same way the browser tracker on a public page needs none. Login only matters when you read data back, and [Authentication](authentication.qmd) covers that.

## Send your first event

```python
response = umami.new_event(
    event_name='purchase-course',
    url='/courses/python-for-absolute-beginners',
    custom_data={'plan': 'individual', 'price': 69},
)
```

`event_name` is the only required argument. `url` defaults to `/` and is the page the event is attributed to, so pick the page a visitor would associate with it. `custom_data` is any JSON-serializable dict and becomes the event's properties in Umami.

If that call returns without raising, Umami accepted the event. Now go and look at it.

## Read the result

Open the website in your Umami dashboard. The event appears in two places:

- In the **Events** section at the bottom of the website page, listed under its `event_name` with a count.
- In the **Pages** section, as traffic on the `url` you passed.

Click the event name to see the properties from `custom_data`. That is the `plan` and `price` you sent, now sitting alongside everything the browser tracker collects.

The return value is Umami's JSON response parsed into a dict. On current Umami versions it holds a `cache` token plus `sessionId` and `visitId`. You can ignore it; the exact keys depend on the server version and the package does not use them.

If the call raised, or returned normally and the dashboard stays stubbornly empty, go to [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd). The empty dashboard has a usual suspect, Umami's bot filter, and the page explains how to catch it.

## Check the connection

`heartbeat()` answers one question: can this process reach the configured instance? It never raises. It returns `False` on any problem, including a missing `set_url_base()`, so it is safe to call from a health check.

```python
if not umami.heartbeat():
    print('Umami is not reachable')
```

## Umami Cloud

On Umami Cloud there is no URL to point at and no password to type. You create an API key in the Cloud dashboard, and that key replaces `set_url_base()`:

```python
import umami

umami.set_cloud_api_key('your-cloud-api-key')  # region='us' or 'eu' is optional
umami.set_website_id('978435e2-7ba1-4337-9860-ec31ece2db60')
umami.set_hostname('example.com')

umami.new_event(event_name='purchase-course', url='/courses/python-for-absolute-beginners')
```

Events go to `https://cloud.umami.is/api/send` and query calls go to `https://api.umami.is/v1`, with the key sent as an `x-umami-api-key` header. Do not call `login()` in Cloud mode; it raises `OperationNotAllowedError`, because the key already is the credential. [Authentication](authentication.qmd) explains both modes and how to switch between them.
